doc.title: Josiah Gluck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 13, 2022

title: SNL shorthand such as RF 15
summary: Gluck shares the code 'RF 15', warning that a band member is within earshot of the control room.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Do you have in-house terms for certain things? I was thinking about today we have someone who’s going to lip-sync although I know it’s rare — I believe it’s rare on Saturday Night Live but I’m just wondering if you developed a vocabulary with your teammates about things?

No I mean you’ll usually know whether or not someone is miming or lip-syncing, which is really not encouraged at all, and then sometimes we’ll have — the one little bit of shorthand — I guess I shouldn’t reveal this — is that someone will say, “Do you have microphone RF 15?” And it’s like, “Yes I do.” Or I’ll say, “I have RF 15 on.” And RF-15 is, we don’t use a microphone named, Radio Microphone 15, it just lets them know somebody from the band is within listening distance or the control room and therefore be careful what you say on the PL. Be careful what you say.
Yes sort of like a live mic somewhere.
A live mic somewhere so they’ll say, “These guys are idiots” it’s like, “Oh, oh they must be talking about other idiots not you guys.” You know so anyway. There goes the dog.
